title: NEXORA connector settings
description: User-facing Connector preferences stored under -nexora.settings. Deliberately narrow: this document holds intentions ('want core auto-start'), never observations ('core is running'), which belong to connector.status and must not be cached here. Anything secret is a keystore reference or lives in another namespace.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this document, migrated independently of -nexora.schemaVersion so a settings change does not force an envelope migration (docs/architecture/35-schema-versioning-migration.md §4).

autoStart.description: Start Xray when the Connector comes up. When false, applying a ConnectorProfile still triggers an on-demand start, because a profile the user selected is intent.

installChannel.description: 'pinned' runs whatever packages/pins.schema.json attests. 'manual' refuses to run anything the Connector did not fetch (docs/architecture/33). There is no 'any version found on disk': a binary chosen by path is a binary chosen by whoever wrote that path.

installRoot.description: Override of the pin's installRoot. Null means use the pin, whose own installRoot is the per-user core directory of doc 34 §7's layout -- %LOCALAPPDATA% (the per-user core directory of doc 34 section 7's layout) in the shipped example -- and the active binary inside it is resolved from the install receipt, never from a directory listing (docs/architecture/33 §7). The supervisor's Launch resolves this path per spawn and the pre-exec proof re-hashes the file it names; a receipt that does not exist is Core not being installed yet, and the answer is a refusal, never a download on the apply path. Paths are not secrets but are not logged either (docs/architecture/32).

core.description: Which Core binary may run and how it gets started. Preferences only; observed state comes from connector.status.

range.description: The only ports a NEXORA-managed Xray may bind. Narrower ranges fail more often on shared machines; wider ones collide with software the user already runs.

host.description: Loopback, not configurable (ADR-0006). A setting that could open the inbound to the LAN is a SOCKS proxy for the whole network with no authentication; core.start refuses to start such a config and this schema refuses to describe one.

persistAssignments.description: Reuse the previous port for the same profile so a Connector restart does not invalidate a chrome.proxy setting the browser already has.

ports.description: The loopback port policy the Compiler allocates from. Host is fixed by schema to 127.0.0.1 (ADR-0006).

logLevel.description: 'debug' additionally logs compiled config structure with every secret field replaced.

retentionDays.description: Ring-buffer age, not a archive. 0 keeps the current session only.

diagnosticsIncludeByDefault.description: Sections diagnostics.get includes when the caller does not ask for specific ones. Names are the command's own include enum (protocol/commands/diagnostics.get.json) and scripts/verify.mjs asserts every name here exists there -- a settings document that invents a section produces a Diagnostics dump with a silently missing half.

telemetry.description: Log verbosity, retention and what diagnostics.get includes by default.

failClosedDefault.description: The global default. Per-profile failOpen is an override the user must confirm; it cannot be expressed as a global setting here, because a product whose default is fail-open has no failure policy.

notificationLevel.description: 'silent' is permitted only for health changes, never for a blocked state: ADR-0009 requires the block to be visible.

proxy.description: Browser-side behaviour on failure. The fail-closed default is not overridable here by design.

allOf.description: Port range must be sane and small enough that the Connector can prove it holds nothing outside loopback.
